name: Mezopharma Hair Cocktail

lead: Mezopharma Hair Cocktail is a retail product sold for hair mesotherapy, in which a blend of vitamins, plant extracts or other actives is placed in the scalp through many tiny injections. The aim is to support hair thickness and scalp condition.
People interested in hair density use cocktails like this alongside or instead of other hair-loss routines. Product-specific published research is not available.

paras: Mesotherapy sessions are performed by a practitioner using fine needles or a device across the scalp, usually as a course of repeated visits. Ingredient lists vary by cocktail and seller.

Wikipedia notes injection-based mesotherapy has been linked to infections and skin abscesses, mostly tied to unhygienic conditions, and that cosmetic uses have not been tested in standard clinical trials.[1]

chain: Cocktail of actives delivered into the scalp
angle.text: Users and sellers describe scalp mesotherapy as a way to support hair thickness. It is typically done in repeated sessions with a practitioner.

lead: Mezopharma Hair Cocktail is a ready-to-use hair mesotherapy blend sold at retail. Mesotherapy is a practice that involves intradermal or subcutaneous injections of substances such as vitamins, plant extracts, hormones and hyaluronic acid.[1]

People use scalp mesotherapy to try to improve hair density and quality. Wikipedia credits Michel Pistor (1924 to 2003) with founding the field and says the French press coined the term in 1958.[1] No published clinical study of this specific product has been identified.

paras: Mesotherapy covers injections of mixtures into the skin and is described in Wikipedia as having poor scientific backing for cosmetic uses; a small study of four facial multivitamin sessions in ten patients found no clinically relevant rejuvenation.[1] Reported problems include skin abscesses and a mycobacterial infection at an Australian salon; a 2011 French ban was lifted after investigators tied the problems to hygiene.[1]
